questions.question: How many cells do large animals have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Billions**__.

__
 
• Animals consist of millions of millions i.e. **Billions of cells.**
 
• Humans consist of more than 40 trillion cells.
 
• Every animal's cell has an important function that helps it survive and thrive.
 
• Animal cells are made up of several parts, called organelles, that work together and enable the cell to function.
 
• An animal cell is eukaryotic in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Animal cells consist of genes that code for particular proteins and mRNA and thus control the cell functions.
 
• It contains outer cell membranes and membrane-bound organelles.
 
• The animal cell does not have any cell wall.
 
• It contains membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, and lysosomes.
 
• It consists of a nucleus and it is present inside the double membrane.
 
• The nucleus is centrally located.
 
• It has Nuclear pores that allow the diffusion of a substance through it.

questions.question: What is the style of sculpture prevalent in Bengal during the period between the ninth and eleventh centuries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pala**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pala style** characterizes sculptures in **Bengal and Bihar** from the **9th to the 11th centuries**, encompassing Bangladesh.
 
• Contrarily, sculptures from the mid-11th to the mid-13th centuries are linked to the Sena rulers.
 
• The Pala era showcases a distinctive sculptural tradition during its time frame.
 
• **Sena rulers**, in contrast, leave their imprint on the sculptural landscape in the subsequent period.
 
• The two styles represent distinct phases in the evolution of sculpture in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style:**

 
 
• The Nagara style is a prominent architectural style in Indian temple construction, primarily associated with **northern India**.
 
• Key features include a** tall shikhara (tower) **above the sanctum, often with a curvilinear or pyramid-like shape.
 
• **Ornate carvings, intricate sculptures, and decorative motifs characterize Nagara temples, reflecting a rich aesthetic**.
 
 
 
• **Panchayatan Style:**
 
 
• The Panchayatan style is a form of temple architecture that involves the construction of a **central main shrine surrounded by four subsidiary shrines**.
 
• Each subsidiary shrine is dedicated to a different deity, and the entire complex is organized in a symmetrical layout.
 
• This style is symbolic of the integration of multiple deities within a single temple structure, demonstrating a holistic approach to worship.
 
 
 
• **Vesara Style:**
 
 
• The Vesara style, also known as the **Deccan or Karnataka** style, is an architectural and sculptural tradition prevalent in the Deccan region of India.
 
• It is a **fusion of both Nagara and Dravida styles**, showcasing a unique blend of features from northern and southern temple architecture.
 
• Characteristics may include a **stepped pyramidal tower, intricate carvings, and a combination of square and octagonal shapes** in the temple structure.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution emphasizes the fundamental duty – “To preserve and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Art 51A (c)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51A is a Fundamental Duty in Part IV -A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The idea of incorporating Fundamental Duties into the Indian constitution was inspired by the Russian Constitution (erstwhile Soviet Union).
 
• They help in promoting the spirit of discipline and patriotism among the citizens.
 
• Additionally, they assist in achieving societal objectives by encouraging active citizen participation instead of the spectator.
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitution Amendment Act in 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Ten duties were originally added, and one more was added in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.

List of 11 Fundamental Duties under article 51 A:

 
• 51A (a): to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• 51A (b): to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
• 51A (c): to uphold and protect** the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. **Hense Option 1 is correct.
 
• 51A (d): to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• 51A (e): to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• 51A (f): to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• 51A (g): to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• 51A (h): to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• 51A (i): to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• 51A (j): to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
 
• 51A (k): who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__Swaran Singh Committee 1976 Report__

 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was formed in 1976 to examine the working of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The committee's objective was to recommend amendments to the Constitution.
 
• The committee submitted its report in 1976, known as the Swaran Singh Committee Report.
 
• The report proposed several amendments to the Constitution.
 
• It recommended changes in fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, emergency provisions, and the role of the President.
 
• One significant proposal was the inclusion of the Right to Property as a legal right.
 
• The committee also recommended strengthening the parliamentary system, enhancing the judiciary's role, and improving political parties' functioning.
 
• However, not all of the committee's recommendations were implemented.
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee Report remains a significant document in the constitutional discourse of India.

questions.question: Which disease refers to the spectrum of ocular disease caused by severe Vitamin A deficiency (VAD)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xerophthalmia**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Xerophthalmia is caused due to a deficiency of vitamin A.__
 
• Xerophthalmia is a condition of early vitamin A deficiency in which the cornea keratinizes, becomes opaque, and forms dry, scaly layers of cells.
 
• The affected cornea is susceptible to infection.
 
• Xerophthalmia can progress to irreversible blindness if left untreated.
 
• Even today, Xerophthalmia is a major problem in developing countries and is a leading cause of preventable blindness.
 
• In the eye, vitamin A is metabolized to form rhodopsin (retinal visual pigment). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Diabetic retinopathy**

__
 
• When a patient with diabetic retinopathy experiences sudden vision changes, the priority is to minimize further damage.
 
• Resting in a darkened room can reduce strain on the eyes and prevent exacerbation of the condition.
 
• Other interventions may be necessary, but immediate comfort and protection of the patient's vision are paramount.
 
• Diabetic retinopathy is a condition that can lead to severe and irreversible vision loss if not promptly managed.

**Glaucoma**​

 
• Glaucoma is not a single ailment/disease it is a group of eye conditions that causes blindness.
 
• There are two types of glaucoma
 
 
• Open-angle glaucoma
 
• Closed-angle glaucoma
 
 

**Cataract**​

 
• It represents a condition or state of cloudiness in the lens of the eye which results in a blurred, distorted or incomplete vision due to the blockage of light__ necessary for having a clear vision.
 
• In this condition, the lens tissue changes and becomes thicker.
 
• Symptoms can include blurred colors, distorted or double vision, luminous halos, and issues related to night vision.
 
• Congenital cataract is a cataract that is present at birth. It occurs when a mother contacts German measles in the first three months of pregnancy.

questions.question: In India, who among the following is in charge of regulating the money supply?

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the controlling authority of money supply in India. The basic functions of the bank have been described in the Preamble of the Reserve Bank of India as follows:
 
• To regulate the issue of banknotes, maintain reserves with a view to achieving monetary stability in India and operate the currency and credit system in the interest of the country in general.
 
• Formulate, implement, and monitor monetary policy.
 
• To regulate and supervise the financial system.
 
• Managing foreign exchange.
 
• Issuing, exchanging currency and destroying them when they are no longer operational.

Thus, the correct answer is the Reserve Bank of India__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__

 __
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of India.
 
• It is the operator of all the banks in India.
 
• The Reserve Bank controls the economy of India.
 
• It was established on 1 April 1935 as per the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934​.
 
• Initially, its headquarters was in Kolkata, which shifted to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• Earlier it was a private bank but since 1949 it has become a Government of India undertaking.

 __

• The responsibility for coinage vests with the Government of India on the basis of the Coinage Act, 2011 as amended from time to time.
 
• The Government of India is also responsible for the designing and minting of coins in various denominations.
 
• 
 
The Government of India in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India decides the design of banknotes.__​__

 
 
 
 
• __**State Bank of India**__
 __
 
• ​SBI was established on **July 1, 1955,** through an Act of Parliament, by merging the** Imperial Bank of India and its then-five subsidiaries.**

 Imperial Bank of India** was founded in 1921 **by European merchants in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• Over the years, SBI has expanded its operations to become one of the largest banks in the world, with a network of over 22,500 branches and ATMs across India and overseas.
 
• SBI is a **public sector bank**, which means that the government of India **owns a majority share in the bank**.
 
• SBI is one of the** leading providers of financial services in India**, including banking, insurance, and investment banking.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides protection to persons arrested or detained under the preventive detention law?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**Article 22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution guarantees certain procedural safeguards to individuals in the** case of arrest and detention** in certain cases.
 
• This article applies to both** citizens and non-citizens**.
 
• This provision extends some procedural safeguards to individuals in the case of arrest.
 
• It comes into play after a person has been arrested. **It is not a fundamental right against arrest and detention**.
 
• The idea behind this right is to prevent arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• This provision provides the following safeguards:
 
 
• **Article 22(1)** - Any person who is in custody must be informed of the grounds for his or her arrest. Additionally, he or she cannot be denied the right to consult with a lawyer.
 
• **Article 22(2)** - The arrested person must be produced before a judicial magistrate within 24 hours of his or her arrest.
 
• **Article 22(3)** - No person arrested under a preventive detention law can be detained for a period longer than the period specified by the judicial magistrate.
 
 
 
• **However, these safeguards do not apply to**:
 
 
• Enemy aliens
 
• Foreigners
 
• Persons arrested under preventive detention laws
 
 

Article 22 of the Indian Constitution **ensures the right not to be subjected to abuse during arrest **or while in custody. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are two types of detention:
 
 
• Penal detention is detention after trial.
 
• Preventive detention is detention without trial.
 
• The idea behind this is to prevent a person from committing a crime. This means that individuals can be detained on suspicion.
 
• The rights of persons arrested in this manner are governed by preventive detention laws.

questions.question: Who stated that the elements' properties are a periodic function of their atomic weights?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Modern Periodic Law was given by Dmitri Mendeleev.
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev stated that "The properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses".
 
• The Modern Periodic Law was modified by Henry Moseley.
 
• Henry Moseley showed that the atomic number is a more fundamental property of an element than its atomic mass.
 
• So, the Modern Periodic Law can be stated that "The physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic number".
 
• Features of Modern Periodic Table:
 
 
• There are eighteen vertical columns known as groups in the modern periodic table which are arranged from left to right and seven horizontal rows which are known as periods.
 
• The elements of groups 1, 2, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 are known as the main group elements or normal elements.
 
• The elements of groups 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, and 12 are known as the transition elements.
 
• Group 18 is called noble gases or inert gases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Johann Dobereiner was the first to consider the idea of trends among properties of elements.
 
• In 1829, he noted a similarity among the physical and chemical properties of several groups of three elements (Triads).
 
• These Triads were called as Dobereiner Triads.
 
• John Alexander Newland profounded the Law of Octaves in 1865.
 
• According to Newland's Law of Octaves when elements are arranged in the order of increasing atomic masses, the properties of the eighth element are a repetition of the properties of the first element.
 
• John Dalton is known for introducing the Atomic Theory in chemistry in the year 1808.
 
• Dalton’s atomic theory proposed that all matter was composed of atoms, indivisible and indestructible building blocks. While all atoms of an element were identical, different elements had atoms of differing size and mass.

questions.question: Which cryptographic technique uses a single key for both encryption and decryption of data?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Symmetric encryption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Symmetric encryption**, also known as **secret key encryption**.
 
• It involves the use of the **same cryptographic key for both the encryption of plaintext and the decryption of ciphertext.**
 
• The keys can either be identical or there may be a simple transformation to transition between the two keys.
 
• Simple symmetric encryption techniques include the** Caesar Cipher,** though this is typically considered easy to decipher with modern computational capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hashing**

 
 
• Hashing is a technique that converts an input of any length into a fixed-size string of text, using a mathematical function.
 
• It is primarily used for data integrity, not for encryption, and it is typically a one-way function, meaning the original data cannot be retrieved from the hash.
 
 
 
• **Public-key encryption**
 
 
• It is also known as asymmetric encryption.
 
• This type of encryption uses a pair of keys - one private and one public.
 
• The public key is used for encryption and the private key is used for decryption.
 
• It is primarily used in scenarios where secure data transmission is required over an insecure network like the Internet.
 
 
 
• **Asymmetric encryption**
 
 
• This is another name for public-key encryption.
 
• It uses two keys, one private and one public, for the encryption and decryption process.
 
• It offers high levels of security but requires greater computational resources than symmetric encryption.

questions.question: Approximately ___________ of the India’s population continued to be employed in agriculture till 1990.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the year **1990**, the **agricultural sector in India** was still the major source of livelihood for about **65% of the population**.
 
• The Green Revolution in the 1960s led to significant increases in agricultural output, which continued to sustain a large part of the Indian population.
 
• Over the years, however, the share of agriculture in India's GDP has been decreasing, despite a majority of the Indian population still being involved in this sector for their livelihood.
 
• **As of 2021, less than 45% **of the population is directly employed in agriculture, indicating a **shift towards more industrial and service occupations**.
 
• Purely agricultural incomes often prove insufficient for many families, resulting in high rates of informal labor and migration towards urban areas.
 
• Government interventions, infrastructure, education, and evolving technology are also shaping the sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Initiated in the** late 1960s, the Green Revolution** was a significant transformation in agriculture facilitated by the mass adoption of** high-yield-variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation systems**.
 
• Targeting major crops like **wheat and rice**, it was aimed at enhancing food production in India and other developing nations.
 
• The Green Revolution immensely **boosted agricultural productivity**, thus elevating farm incomes, alleviating food shortages, and driving economic growth.
 
• However, it had complex effects on agricultural employment.
 
• On one hand, the **increased intensity of farming **(with more crops per year), changed cropping patterns, and a necessity for labor in handling HYV crops and machinery potentially elevated the demand for labor, and thus employment.
 
• It also paved the way for ancillary sectors like **agro-processing, fertilizers, machinery, etc., thereby creating jobs indirectly**.
 
• On the other hand, the capital-intensive nature of the Green Revolution **favored larger farmers**, widening inequality.
 
• Small and marginal farmers often couldn't bear the costs of high-tech inputs, leading to a **consolidation of land and increased labor displacement**.
 
• This swelling of landless laborers without adequate non-farm opportunities has persisted as a critical rural issue.

questions.question: The Bengal Famine took a huge toll of life and was called as tragedy in unpreparedness. In which year did it occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1943**__.

__
 
• The **Bengal Famine of 1943**, was a** catastrophic event in the Bengal province** of British India **during World War II**.
 
• An estimated** 2.1–3 million**, out of a population of 60.3 million people,** died of starvation, malaria, or other diseases exacerbated by malnutrition, population displacement, unsanitary conditions, and lack of healthcare.**
 
• While natural disasters like cyclones and crop diseases contributed to the initial food scarcity, the **Wartime policies of the British colonial administration worsened its impact**.
 
• This included the **'denial policy', **which involved the removal or destruction of boats, bullock carts, or any other means of transport to prevent them from falling into Japanese hands if they invaded India, effectively disrupting distribution networks.
 
• It resulted in enormous loss of life and demonstrated the imperial government's lack of provision for its subjects in times of extreme peril. 
 
• It **led to major shifts in policy and a reconsideration of agricultural and famine relief strategies**, both in the immediate aftermath and after India's independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Madras Famine of 1876 - 1878** was a catastrophic event.
 
• It affected the **Madras Presidency in British India**, now a large part of southern India.
 
• It was part of the larger Indian Famine of 1876–78 that spread across various Indian regions, resulting from severe drought, cyclones and ineffective government policies.
 
• It led to dire food shortages and widespread deaths due to starvation.
 
• The Famine Commission of 1880, sparked by the tragedy, ultimately led to systemic changes, shaping India's future famine prevention strategies.
 
• Thus, the Madras famine was not only a humanitarian disaster but also a poignant moment in India's colonial history, influencing future policy reform.

• **Lord Canning:(1856-1862)****​**
 
 
• **Canning** served as the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857, a major armed uprising against British rule in India.
 
• He is credited with having played a key role in suppressing the rebellion and restoring British control over India, but his administration was also criticized for its harsh repression of the rebels.
 
• Canning initiated a number of social and economic reforms in India, including the introduction of the Indian Civil Service, the establishment of the first universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, and the abolition of the Indian caste system in government employment.
